da-non-sequitur.evidence: S↔P: the core is correct. tr_M = Σ_λ y_λ χ^λ, evaluated at 1, gives Σ d_λ y_λ = tr_M(1) = 1 (prf:2-16). Two problems. (1) Missing q-range. The statement is "over a field R with parameter q ≠ 0" (md:2-3), but the decomposition tr_M = Σ y_λ χ^λ needs H_n(R,q) semisimple, i.e. q² not a primitive e-th root of unity with 2 ≤ e ≤ n. The convention-D Markov parameter z = q³/(q²+1) also needs q² ≠ −1. At q = i (char 0) z is undefined and H_2 is not semisimple ([2]_q = q + q⁻¹ = 0). (2) The classical-limit sentence is false under convention D: "At q = 1 the Markov weights reduce to y_λ = d_λ/n!" (prf:21). Exact counterexample, n = 2, q = 1: z_D = 1/2, so tr_M(σ) = 1/2 = y_(2)·1 + y_(1,1)·(−1), with y_(2) + y_(1,1) = 1. That gives y_(2) = 3/4 and y_(1,1) = 1/4, not d_λ/2! = 1/2. The cited `plancherel_via_recipe` "concludes `(1 : ℝ) = 1`" per the ts note (ts:31-33), so it does not establish "Plancherel completeness … for every n" (prf:17-19).
